hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Bangladesh on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Bangladesh on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Bangladesh?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Bangladesh on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Bangladesh article.

questions.proof: Bangladesh has land borders with India on the north, west, and east, and Myanmar on the southeast.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Bangladesh?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Bangladesh article.

questions.proof: Dhaka is the capital and the biggest city.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Dhaka?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Bangladesh is Dhaka.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Bangladesh about 147,570 square kilometres; Sri Lanka about 65,610 square kilometres; East Timor about 14,919 square kilometres; Palau about 466 square kilometres.
